messages:
maria: Nightly evals are failing intermittently on the quantized job. Harness marks worker as TIMED OUT but the child process shows as still alive or exited 0 later. Anyone seen this pattern?

aj: Yep, saw a spike at ~03:12 UTC. Infra logs have a bunch of 'watchdog killed worker' messages.

infra-bot: deployed watchdog v2.3 to eval-cluster-7 at 2026-03-19T03:00:01Z (rollout-id: rdw-watchdog-20260319).

simon: Can you paste the harness log snippet and the child process ps tree if you have it?

maria: Pasting the tail of the harness log we captured:

```
2026-03-19T03:11:58Z harness[pid=4552]: start run quantized/int8/model-x
2026-03-19T03:16:58Z watchdog[pid=4610]: no heartbeat from worker 4556 for 300s, sending SIGTERM
2026-03-19T03:16:59Z kernel: pid=4556 exited code=0
2026-03-19T03:17:00Z harness[pid=4552]: MARKED TIMEOUT (300s) for run quantized/int8/model-x
2026-03-19T03:17:05Z harness[pid=4552]: collecting artifacts
```

We also saw the child process (4556) listed as exited with code 0 in the kernel logs, but the harness still marked a timeout earlier. There's a ~1s discrepancy between SIGTERM and kernel exit, but harness decided timeout first.

aj: Huh. That smells like a PTY or stdout buffering issue where harness blocks waiting for child's stdout and decides it's hung. We've seen similar with pty.spawn where the master fd gets into a weird state.

simon: Is this specific to quantized runs (int8)? Any env differences like larger batch sizes or streaming enabled?

maria: So far mostly the int8/quantized test matrix. FP32 runs aren't showing it. Quantized ones have slightly longer sampling loops (more batched decode), so more stdout churn.

aj: I can try running with strace and also add a small wrapper to call waitpid explicitly rather than relying on the pty read to detect process exit. If waitpid returns, harness should treat it as completion even if pty still has buffered data.

infra-bot: scheduled job nightly-eval-quantized-repro #2147 on cluster-7, expected start in 6m.

eval-bot: Note: current harness semantics treat lack of output for > timebox as TIMED_OUT even if child later exits. This is by design for now to avoid stuck runs.

simon: That policy makes sense, but here the policy is too eager because the child actually exits cleanly shortly after the cutoff. Two possibilities: 1) harness uses output activity to drive liveness and misses process exit, or 2) pty master is blocking and redispatching events.

maria: Repro steps I used locally: `./run_harness --config quantized-small --worker-isolate --seed 42` — on a subset of prompts it fails within ~10-20 runs. I can reproduce ~30% on my laptop. Logs uploaded to /mnt/eval-repro/214365/maria.tar.gz

aj: Plan: (1) add waitpid-based reaping in harness as a fallback, (2) log open fds/pty state on timeout, (3) add a short grace window (30s) to allow stdout flush before declaring TIMED_OUT. I'll open a hotfix PR.

simon: Sounds good. If we can reliably repro, let's also capture strace of the child and a pty dump. Aj, please include a debug flag that leaves the pty master open and writes its buffers to file.

aj: Will do. I'll also add a small test that simulates a child that exits but delays stdout flush and ensure harness treats it as success when waitpid shows exit.

maria: Assigning ownership: aj -> hotfix and PR, maria -> repro artifacts and logs, simon -> review and validation on cluster. Infra to monitor the scheduled job. @aj please tag me when upload is ready. :thumbsup:

simon: Thanks — ping me once PR is up. We'll coordinate a canary cut after fix. :eyes:

maria: Upload complete: /mnt/eval-repro/214365/maria.tar.gz. Triggered nightly job last night with debug=true and attached pty-dumps. I'll post links in thread when indexing finishes.
